segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַמְקַנֵּא לְאִשְׁתּוֹ עַל יְדֵי אֲנָשִׁים הַרְבֵּה וּמְצוֹרָע שֶׁנִּתְנַגַּע נְגָעִים הַרְבֵּה,
segments.en: «MISHNA:» The mishna continues to list the five situations in which one offering is brought to atone for several transgressions: Third, «one who issues a warning to his wife» declaring himself jealous «with regard to several» different «men» with whom he suspects her of committing adultery, and forbidding her to be alone with them. If the wife was then found separately in seclusion with each of the men, he brings her to the Temple with one single meal offering of jealousy. «And» fourth, «a leper who was afflicted» with «several» instances of «leprosy,» meaning that he was purified from his leprosy, and before he brought his offerings, he suffered a relapse of the leprosy. When he is finally purified, he brings only one set of offerings.

segments.he: הֵבִיא צִיפֳּרִין וְנִתְנַגֵּעַ – לֹא עָלוּ לוֹ עַד שֶׁיָּבִיא חַטָּאתוֹ, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁיָּבִיא אֲשָׁמוֹ.
segments.en: If a leper «brought» the two requisite «birds» on the first day of his purification (see Leviticus 14:4–7), «and» prior to bringing his offerings on the eighth day of his purification he «was afflicted» with a relapse of leprosy, those birds «do not satisfy his obligation until he brings his sin offering. Rabbi Yehuda says: Until he brings his guilt offering.»

moves.summary: Jealousy warnings about many men, and a leper afflicted many times, bring one offering
Birds brought then relapse: not credited until the sin offering
